goal: Fix what the 2026-11-11 review found in the kit: installed-plugin drift, doctor, the smoke test, standardized public driver descriptions, input paths for interpretation, splitting interpretation into smaller tasks, service diagnosability and robustness, and packages that stop verifying after a runtime edit. Benchmark items are out: they are recorded in .scratch and move to a new repository.

escalation.reason: Feature 01, 01-B12 on Windows. doctor launches the configured Codex command directly, while a start on Windows launches it through _windows_worker.py from the stage workspace. A configured command that is a relative path with a directory part (for example tools/codex) can therefore answer doctor's check and be reported available on Windows although a start would not find it, and the test for that case is skipped on Windows. The Spec does not settle it: 01-B3 gives an answering command reason null, while 01-B12 says a relative command's reason must say the path must be absolute. Options: (a) accept the Windows gap; (b) launch the check through the Windows wrapper as a start does, which cannot be run on this machine; (c) report any relative command with a directory part as unavailable on every platform without launching it, with 01-B12 taking precedence over 01-B3. The review otherwise passed every Deviation and the check printed PASS. Two Standards must-fixes wait for the next fix round: the ValueError message at src/generative_driver/setup.py:102 names no offending value, and the docs of the helpers program, codex_on_path and stand_in in tests/test_doctor.py do not lead with what they return.
